title: Function template instantiation
recap: A template definition is a recipe; a call or explicit request causes the needed specialization to be instantiated. Type arguments may be deduced from arguments or supplied explicitly.
A template that compiles for one type can fail or narrow for another. Test several instantiations, especially a wide integer and a floating-point value.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement squared<T>(value) by returning value*value as T. Support explicit and deduced instantiations for int, long long, and double. Tested values and products fit their types. Do not store the result in a fixed int intermediate.
hints: Keep arithmetic in the parameter type.
The result of long long multiplication must not pass through int.
